In [[mathematics]], more precisely in [[group theory]] and [[hyperbolic geometry]], '''Arithmetic Kleinian groups''' are a special class of [[Kleinian group]]s constructed using [[Order (ring theory)|order]]s in [[quaternion algebra]]s. They are particular instances of [[arithmetic group]]s. An '''arithmetic hyperbolic three-manifold''' is the quotient of [[hyperbolic space]] <math>\mathbb H^3</math> by an arithmetic Kleinian group.

== Definition and examples ==

=== Quaternion algebras ===
{{Main| Quaternion algebra}}

A quaternion algebra over a field <math>F</math> is a four-dimensional [[Central simple algebra|central simple]] <math>F</math>-algebra. A quaternion algebra has a basis <math>1, i, j, ij</math> where <math>i^2, j^2 \in F^\times</math> and <math>ij = -ji</math>.

A quaternion algebra is said to be split over <math>F</math> if it is isomorphic as an <math>F</math>-algebra to the algebra of matrices <math>M_2(F)</math>; a quaternion algebra over an [[algebraically closed field]] is always split.

If <math>\sigma</math> is an embedding of <math>F</math> into a field <math>E</math> we shall denote by <math>A \otimes_\sigma E</math> the algebra obtained by [[Extension of scalars|extending scalars]] from <math>F</math> to <math>E</math> where we view <math>F</math> as a subfield of <math>E</math> via <math>\sigma</math>.

=== Arithmetic Kleinian groups ===

A subgroup of <math>\mathrm{PGL}_2(\Complex)</math> is said to be ''derived from a quaternion algebra'' if it can be obtained through the following construction. Let <math>F</math> be a [[number field]] which has exactly two embeddings into <math>\Complex</math> whose image is not contained in <math>\Reals</math> (one conjugate to the other). Let <math>A</math> be a quaternion algebra over <math>F</math> such that for any embedding <math>\tau: F \to \Reals</math> the algebra <math>A \otimes_\tau \Reals</math> is isomorphic to the [[Hamilton quaternions]]. Next we need an order <math>\mathcal O</math> in <math>A</math>. Let <math>\mathcal O^1</math> be the group of elements in <math>\mathcal O</math> of reduced norm 1 and let <math>\Gamma</math> be its image in <math>M_2(\Complex)</math> via <math>\phi</math>. We then consider the Kleinian group obtained as the image in <math>\mathrm{PGL}_2(\Complex)</math> of <math>\phi(\mathcal O^1)</math>.

The main fact about these groups is that they are discrete subgroups and they have finite covolume for the [[Haar measure]] on <math>\mathrm{PGL}_2(\Complex)</math>. Moreover, the construction above yields a cocompact subgroup [[if and only if]] the algebra <math>A</math> is not split over <math>F</math>. The discreteness is a rather immediate consequence of the fact that <math>A</math> is only split at its complex embeddings. The finiteness of covolume is harder to prove.{{sfn|Maclachlan|Reid|2003|loc=Theorem 8.1.2}}

An ''arithmetic Kleinian group'' is any subgroup of <math>\mathrm{PGL}_2(\Complex)</math> which is [[commensurability (group theory)|commensurable]] to a group derived from a quaternion algebra. It follows immediately from this definition that arithmetic Kleinian groups are discrete and of finite covolume (this means that they are [[Lattice (discrete subgroup)|lattices]] in <math>\mathrm{PGL}_2(\Complex)</math>).

=== Examples ===

Examples are provided by taking <math>F</math> to be an [[imaginary quadratic field]], <math>A = M_2(F)</math> and <math>\mathcal O = M_2(O_F)</math> where <math>O_F</math> is the [[ring of integers]] of <math>F</math> (for example <math>F = \Q(i)</math> and <math>O_F = \Z[i]</math>). The groups thus obtained are the [[Bianchi group]]s. They are not cocompact, and any arithmetic Kleinian group which is not commensurable to a conjugate of a Bianchi group is cocompact.

If <math>A</math> is any quaternion algebra over an imaginary quadratic number field <math>F</math> which is not isomorphic to a matrix algebra then the unit groups of orders in <math>A</math> are cocompact.

== Trace field of arithmetic manifolds ==

The invariant [[trace field]] of a Kleinian group (or, through the monodromy image of the fundamental group, of an hyperbolic manifold) is the field generated by the traces of the squares of its elements. In the case of an arithmetic manifold whose fundamental groups is commensurable with that of a manifold derived from a quaternion algebra over a number field <math>F</math> the invariant trace field equals <math>F</math>.

One can in fact characterise arithmetic manifolds through the traces of the elements of their fundamental group. A Kleinian group is an arithmetic group if and only if the following three conditions are realised:
*Its invariant trace field <matH>F</math> is a number field with exactly one complex place; 
*The traces of its elements are [[algebraic integer]]s; 
*For any <math>\gamma</math> in the group, <math>t=\mathrm{Trace}(\gamma^2)</math> and any embedding <math>\sigma: F \to \R</math> we have <math>|\sigma(t)| \le 2</math>.

== Geometry and spectrum of arithmetic hyperbolic three-manifolds ==

=== Volume formula ===

For the volume of an arithmetic three manifold <math>M = \Gamma_{\mathcal O} \backslash \mathbb H^3</math> derived from a maximal order in a quaternion algebra <math>A</math> over a number field <math>F</math>, we have this formula:{{sfn|Maclachlan|Reid|2003|loc=Theorem 11.1.3}}
<math display="block"> \mathrm{vol}(M) =  \frac {2 |D_F|^{\frac 3 2} \cdot \zeta_F(2)} {2^{2r + 1} \cdot \pi^{2r}} \cdot \prod_{\mathfrak p | D_A} (N(\mathfrak p) - 1). </math>
where <math>D_A,D_F</math> are the [[discriminant]]s of <math>A, F</math> respectively; <math>\zeta_F</math> is the [[Dedekind zeta function]] of <math>F</math>; and <math>r = [F:\Q]</math>.

=== Finiteness results ===

A consequence of the volume formula in the previous paragraph is that
{{block indent | em = 1.5 | text = ''Given <math>v > 0</math> there are at most finitely many arithmetic hyperbolic 3-manifolds with volume less than <math>v</math>.''}}

This is in contrast with the fact that [[hyperbolic Dehn surgery]] can be used to produce infinitely many non-isometric hyperbolic 3-manifolds with bounded volume. In particular, a corollary is that given a cusped hyperbolic manifold, at most finitely many Dehn surgeries on it can yield an arithmetic hyperbolic manifold.

=== Remarkable arithmetic hyperbolic three-manifolds ===

The [[Weeks manifold]] is the hyperbolic three-manifold of smallest volume<ref>{{cite journal | last=Milley | first=Peter | title=Minimum volume hyperbolic 3-manifolds. | journal=Journal of Topology | volume=2 | year=2009 | pages=181–192 | mr=2499442 | doi=10.1112/jtopol/jtp006| arxiv=0809.0346 | s2cid=3095292 }}</ref> and the [[Meyerhoff manifold]] is the one of next smallest volume.

The complement in the three-sphere of the [[figure-eight knot (mathematics)|figure-eight knot]] is an arithmetic hyperbolic three-manifold<ref>{{cite journal | last=Riley | first=Robert | title=A quadratic parabolic group | journal=[[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]] | volume=77 | issue=2 | year=1975 | pages=281–288 | mr=0412416 | doi=10.1017/s0305004100051094| bibcode=1975MPCPS..77..281R }}</ref> and attains the smallest volume among all cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Cao | first1=Chun | last2=Meyerhoff |first2=G. Robert | title=The orientable cusped hyperbolic 3-manifolds of minimum volume | journal=Inventiones Mathematicae | volume=146 | issue=3 | year=2001 | pages=451–478 | mr=1869847 | doi=10.1007/s002220100167| bibcode=2001InMat.146..451C | s2cid=123298695 }}</ref>

=== Spectrum and Ramanujan conjectures ===

The [[Ramanujan conjecture]] for automorphic forms on <math>\mathrm{GL}(2)</math> over a number field would imply that for any congruence cover of an arithmetic three-manifold (derived from a quaternion algebra) the spectrum of the Laplace operator is contained in <math>[1, +\infty)</math>.

== Arithmetic manifolds in three-dimensional topology ==

Many of Thurston's conjectures (for example the [[virtually Haken conjecture]]), now all known to be true following the work of [[Ian Agol]],<ref>{{cite journal | first=Ian | last=Agol |author-link=Ian Agol| title=The virtual Haken conjecture | others=With an appendix by Ian Agol, Daniel Groves, and Jason Manning | journal=Documenta Mathematica | year=2013 | pages=1045–1087 | volume=18 | mr=3104553 | url=https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/documenta/vol-18/33.html }}</ref> were checked first for arithmetic manifolds by using specific methods.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lackenby | first1=Marc | last2=Long | first2=Darren D. | last3=Reid | first3=Alan W. | title=Covering spaces of arithmetic 3-orbifolds | journal=[[International Mathematics Research Notices]] | volume=2008 | year=2008|mr=2426753|doi=10.1093/imrn/rnn036| arxiv=math/0601677 }}</ref> In some arithmetic cases the Virtual Haken conjecture is known by general means but it is not known if its solution can be arrived at by purely arithmetic means (for instance, by finding a congruence subgroup with positive first Betti number).

Arithmetic manifolds can be used to give examples of manifolds with large injectivity radius whose first Betti number vanishes.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Calegari| first1=Frank | last2=Dunfield | first2=Nathan | title=Automorphic forms and rational homology 3-spheres | journal=[[Geometry & Topology]] | volume=10 | year=2006 | pages=295–329 | doi=10.2140/gt.2006.10.295| arxiv=math/0508271|mr=2224458 | s2cid=5506430 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boston | first1=Nigel | last2=Ellenberg | first2=Jordan |author2-link= Jordan Ellenberg|title=Pro-p groups and towers of rational homology spheres | journal=[[Geometry & Topology]] | volume=10 | year=2006 | pages=331–334 | doi=10.2140/gt.2006.10.331| arxiv=0902.4567|mr=2224459 | s2cid=14889934 }}</ref>

A remark by [[William Thurston]] is that arithmetic manifolds "...often seem to have special beauty."<ref>{{cite journal| last=Thurston | first=William | author-link=William Thurston|date=1982 | title=Three-dimensional manifolds, Kleinian groups and hyperbolic geometry | url=https://www.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=648524 | journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume=6 | issue=3 | pages=357–381 | doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1982-15003-0| doi-access=free }}</ref> This can be substantiated by results showing that the relation between topology and geometry for these manifolds is much more predictable than in general. For example:
*For a given genus ''g'' there are at most finitely many arithmetic (congruence) hyperbolic 3-manifolds which fiber over the circle with a fiber of genus ''g''.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Biringer | first1=Ian | last2=Souto | first2=Juan | title=A finiteness theorem for hyperbolic 3-manifolds | journal=Journal of the London Mathematical Society |series=Second Series | volume=84 | pages=227–242 | year=2011 | doi=10.1112/jlms/jdq106| arxiv=0901.0300 | s2cid=11488751 }}</ref>
*There are at most finitely many arithmetic (congruence) hyperbolic 3-manifolds with a given Heegaard genus.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Gromov | first1=Misha | author1-link = Mikhail Leonidovich Gromov | last2=Guth | first2=Larry | author2-link = Larry Guth | title=Generalizations of the Kolmogorov-Barzdin embedding estimates | journal=Duke Mathematical Journal | volume=161 | pages=2549–2603 | year=2012 | issue=13 | doi=10.1215/00127094-1812840| arxiv=1103.3423 | s2cid=7295856 }}</ref>
